headline: macOS 27 Golden Gate rolls out with new Siri AI features
summary: Apple's latest Mac OS update is now available, bringing a revamped Siri with AI capabilities and new Safari tab organization. However, some advanced features require newer M3 Macs.
details: Apple has officially released macOS 27 Golden Gate, bringing significant AI enhancements to Macs. The update, announced at WWDC in June, is now available for download on compatible devices.

The headline feature is the integration of Siri AI, Apple's most ambitious attempt to embed artificial intelligence deeply into its desktop operating system. This new Siri boasts features like dedicated app integration, screen awareness, automatic proofreading, and personal context.

Under the hood, Siri AI is powered by Apple's new Foundation Models, which leverage Google Gemini technology for advanced natural language processing, computer vision, and image generation. This aims to provide a more robust AI experience for Mac users.

However, access to the full suite of Siri AI features is not universal. Advanced capabilities, including improved Voice Mode, are exclusive to M3 Macs or newer models with at least 12 GB of RAM. This excludes older MacBooks and many MacBook Airs from before 2024.

Furthermore, Siri AI is currently English-only and faces regulatory hurdles in the EU and China, delaying its availability in those regions. The feature is also being rolled out gradually, with many users still on a waitlist.

Siri AI is designed to be systemwide, accessible via a right-click context menu or integrated into Spotlight search. Users can prompt Siri directly on selected files in Finder or ask questions within Spotlight, which will automatically launch a Siri chat window.

Visual Intelligence is another key aspect, allowing Siri to analyze screenshots and perform actions based on image content. This integration aims to make AI assistance more context-aware and proactive.

Safari also receives a significant AI-powered update with 'Topics,' a new feature for organizing browser tabs. Safari will now automatically group tabs into topics, which can be managed or saved as tab groups, simplifying browsing for users with many open tabs.
